Widebody Mercedes-AMG C 63 Cabrio Is the Perfect CLE Antidote
10 photos
Photo: Instagram | priordesign
The modern-day Mercedes-AMG C 63 may not be the first choice in its class when it comes to real petrolheads, as some of them still cannot get over the fact that it features a four-banger under the hood.
Mind you, it may indeed be a 2.0-liter turbocharged four-cylinder engine that powers it, but it features electric assistance, and the total output and torque are definitely on the impressive side of things. It has 671 horsepower (680 ps/500 kW) and 752 pound-feet (1,020 Nm) of torque combined, and from 0-60 mph (0-97 kph), it is quicker than some old supercar icons, including the Ferrari Enzo. The sprint is dealt with in just 3.3 seconds, in case you forgot.
As for its predecessor, it came with a V8 engine, and it was none other than the ubiquitous 4.0-liter bi-turbo mill that powered it. The C 63 had 469 hp (476 ps/350 kW) and 480 lb-ft (650 Nm) of torque to play with, and the C 63 S came with 500 hp (510 ps/380 kW) and 520 lb-ft (700 Nm) of torque. It needed just under 4 seconds to hit 62 mph (100 kph) from rest in both cases, with the S being slightly quicker, obviously, and the top speed was electronically capped at 155 and 180 mph (250-280 kph), respectively.
Now, we haven’t mentioned the previous-generation Mercedes-AMG C 63 for nothing, because it is the star of the show in this story. Actually, that is due to Prior Design, which recently put the spotlight on a tuned example. As you can clearly see from the images shared in the gallery, it is none other than the open-top model that gets the spotlight here, and for a very good reason, because it has been equipped with a widebody kit signed by the quoted tuner.
Photo: Instagram | priordesign The bundle is called the PD65CC Widebody Kit for the Mercedes- AMG C 63 Cabrio (A205) by Prior Design , and includes a few things that make it shine a lot more. So, what is new, you ask? Well the front and rear wheel arch attachments, for instance, which make this model look like a veritable Black Series. The side skirts are also new, and the front bumper looks like the stock one to us, but it has been modified, and is now a bit more aggressive than before.
The Panamericana grille has also come from Prior Design’s shelves, and so has the apron, which follows the same shape as the lower part of the front bumper. The hood, on the other hand, carries over. There is new special trim on the front fenders. The skirt at the rear and the ducktail spoiler are other novelties, just like the blacked-out badges on the outside, which contribute to the makeover.
We are by no means wheel experts, but it seems that those V-shaped alloys are new. And to be honest, no tuning job these days would be complete without an aftermarket set of wheels. The alloys in question seem to be a bit larger than the OEM ones , and they have been shod in sticky rubber from what we can tell. This build features a white paint finish, has black contrasting elements, and red brake calipers.
Photo: Instagram | priordesign The cockpit is also visible in the images that Prior Design recently shared on its social media channels, and it is mostly black, mixing leather and Alcantara upholstery. There are also some metal accents, and likely some carbon trim on the inside, and it seems that white stitching has also been used inside this old Mercedes-AMG C 63 Cabriolet for more contrast.
According to the tuner, the PD65CC kit mentioned above has been developed especially for the C205 C-Class Coupe, including the C 43 , C 63, and C 63 S versions from Mercedes-AMG. And Prior Design invites interested parties to contact them about the fitment to the open-top model, and recommends “ professional fitting and painting. ”
You might be wondering how much it costs to make your Mercedes premium compact car from this era look like this, and you are not the only ones, because so are we. But in order to find out, you will have to reach out to the tuner directly, and that’s how you will learn other details about it. And don’t forget to drop a line below if you find out the pricing, because we definitely want to know this aspect.
Now, there is no doubt that to the untrained eye, this Mercedes-AMG C 63 Cabrio looks like a veritable Black Series model, and that’s why I absolutely adore it. The model rocks the PD65CC Widebody Kit perfectly, and it easily looks like it could have come directly from the factory looking like this, doesn’t it? But do you dig the aftermarket design, too, or do you think that it is a bit too much? Tell us all about it in the comments area below. The 143 Is a Benchmark Vehicles Camper Van That Blurs the Line Between Rugged and Refined
19 photos
Photo: Benchmark Vehicles
Meet 143, a project based on a 2026 AWD Mercedes-Benz Sprinter 3500 XD with a 170" wheelbase. It's one of the latest builds by Benchmark Vehicles, a Portland, Oregon-based company specializing in custom adventure vehicles, mostly based on vans but also other types of vehicles. This project's name explanation is simple – this is the company's 143rd build.
Benchmark Vehicles creates super capable mobile homes – we've covered some of them here on autoevolution, like this family-friendly rig . Since the company applied the same design philosophy with the 143, you can tell that this is a roam-ready mobile home.
For starters, the van rides on Owl Vans Talon wheels wrapped in BFGoodrich KO3 all-terrain tires. The builders went even further in improving the vehicle's off-roading capabilities by installing an Agile Offroad ride improvement package with Fox shocks and Bilstein struts.
Off-roading can be quite tough on a vehicle – that's why Benchmark Vehicles added some extra protection. First, it applied an XPEL clear matte PPF (paint protection film) wrap to the body. Second, it covered the side rocker panels and part of the front bumper in truck bed liner.
Benchmark Vehicles made sure this van can go further by replacing the stock fuel tank with an S&B 40-gallon (151-liter) fuel tank.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Benchmark Vehicles At the front, you'll come across grille-mounted TripleR lights and an FVC (Flatline Van Co.) bumper complete with a skid plate and a Warn Evo VR12S winch rated for 12,000 lb. (5,447 kg). What's more, there are two solar panels mounted on the hood for a total capacity of 245 W.
The opposite end was also put to great use. A spare tire carrier/ladder combo sits on the left side, while a large carrier with a cargo box takes up the right side. Moreover, underneath, there's a Van Compass Rear Rug step bumper.
Climb on top of the van, and you'll find a large Paragon Offroad rack. It holds a front-facing 50-inch Rigid light bar, a Starlink antenna, solar panels, and a 12-foot Girard power awning. Together with the hood solar panels, the total capacity stands at 416 W.
Other notable mods are Owl Vans side steps, power and water hookups (with plugs for both EU and US), and flares. Flares, also known as pods or capsules, are designed to increase the van width.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Benchmark Vehicles Normally, builders do that to allow you to fit a bed inside in an east to west arrangement instead of the normal north to south. In this van, however, that's not the case – they create some space beside the bed to store things. This rig's flares are also paint matched to the van's body and come with Arctic Tern awning-style windows.
Enter, and you'll be surrounded by a large, almost apartment-like interior. Benchmark Vehicles shared that its interior department was tested to its limit on this Sprinter because of the complexity of the personalized design the customer wanted. This is the customer's third Sprinter, so they knew exactly what they wanted.
The interior has an open layout, with no wall separating the driver's cabin from the rest of the living space. What's more, the driver and passenger seats are mounted on swivel bases, so they can be turned around to face the back of the van and used after you've parked.
Regarding aesthetics, the customer opted for laminated cabinetry with a grain finish, grey woven flooring, and a cream-colored ceiling with matching walls. The look is complemented by white solid surface countertops and black accents, such as the cabinet and drawer handles.
Photo: Benchmark Vehicles Straight ahead as you enter, you'll come across a sizeable counter. It has a large top and a cabinet. Above, you'll find a swiveling fan and a decently sized cabinet.
Next, we have the kitchen, which is split into two units. The unit on the passenger side offers all the meal prep space you need thanks to its super long countertop. It also features a deep stainless steel sink with a pull-out faucet, a slide-out housing a coffee machine, and a portable stove.
The unit on the opposite side houses an overhead cabinet, a tall fridge with a freezer compartment, and a drawer at the bottom. A variety of storage compartments are available in the kitchen, including two overhead cabinets and seven drawers.
For storing clothes, you can use a floor-to-ceiling unit integrating two closets with hanging space.
Photo: Benchmark Vehicles Just like most deluxe camper vans, this Sprinter comes with a bathroom, hidden behind a tall conventional door. It boasts a shower with a handheld wand, a tiny corner shelf, and a Trelino composting toilet. Moreover, the back wall has a window and two L-Tracks for hanging clothes and towels.
This van has the perfect setup for relaxing after a long day out – you'll discover that the rear part of the living space is taken up by a huge king-size bed. The bedroom also offers two reading lights and charging points.
Finally, a roomy garage sits underneath the bedroom and is accessible from both inside and outside the van. In the middle, it offers a pull-out tray attached to heavy-duty slides that makes it easier to load and unload your items.
The garage's sides are partly taken up by two large boxes that accommodate the utility systems. Power is on the left side – the electrical system's highlights are a 3,000 W inverter and a battery bank with a capacity of just under 1,000 Ah.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Benchmark Vehicles As for plumbing, the van is equipped with a 35-gallon (132-liter) freshwater tank with heating pads mounted underneath the vehicle and not one but two under-mounted greywater tanks, also heated. A propane canister sits under the van, beside the freshwater tank.
There are two more important systems in this rig. The first is a diesel-powered Espar heater that provides heated air and water and also powers a radiant floor heating system. The second is a Nomadic Cooling X3 A/C unit.
All in all, the 143 by Benchmark Vehicles combines serious off-road capability with a cozy, four-season-ready living space. Its interior design not only makes a lot of sense functionality-wise but it also makes you feel like you're in an actual home on wheels.

Yamaha is expanding its electric scooter lineup with the new XENTER E, a 125cc-equivalent electric scooter designed specifically with European city riding in mind.
Unveiled around EICMA 2026 in Milan alongside the new NMAX E , the XENTER E is a high-wheel scooter riding on 16-inch wheels front and rear.
That’s an important distinction in European cities, where larger wheels can make quick work of the cobblestones, potholes, and tram tracks that can turn smaller-wheeled scooters into teeth-rattling experiences.
The XENTER E uses Yamaha’s new eAxle powertrain, combining the motor, controller, and reduction gearbox into a compact frame-mounted unit. The motor produces 7.5 kW (10 hp) of peak power and 33.3 Nm of torque, putting the scooter into Europe’s A1 license category.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Mounting the motor to the frame also means Yamaha can use a more conventional motorcycle-style swingarm rather than hanging the motor on the rear suspension like many scooters. That reduces unsprung weight and should help improve handling and ride quality.
Power is supplied from an integrated 3.5 kWh battery mounted low in the chassis. Yamaha claims 108 km (67 miles) of range on the WMTC Class 1 cycle, though real-world range is expected to be somewhat lower.
An 800W onboard charger can refill the battery in around 5.5 hours from a public charging station. Yamaha will also offer a cable for charging from a household outlet.
Other niceties include three riding modes, traction control, regenerative braking, a reverse mode for maneuvering at low speeds, smart-key operation, and a 5-inch TFT display. Smartphone connectivity adds navigation, battery information, maintenance reminders, and parking-location tracking.
There’s also enough underseat storage for a full-face helmet, depending on its size, plus USB-C charging and provisions for accessories such as a windscreen and 34-liter top case.
The XENTER E shares its powertrain and battery with Yamaha’s new NMAX E , but the high-wheel layout gives it a distinctly more European commuter flavor.
Yamaha hasn’t officially announced pricing for each market, though early reports from Milan point to €7,799 in Germany. Deliveries are expected to begin in spring 2027.
It’s certainly not cheap, but the XENTER E looks like Yamaha is finally getting serious about building electric scooters that can replace its bread-and-butter 125cc urban machines, rather than simply supplement them.

Virtual BMW 3 Series G50 Returns to the Beloved 'Round' Angel Eyes, Though Only in Fantasy Land
6 photos
Photo: kelsonik / Instagram
The premium Bavarian automaker BMW has a lot of Neue Klasse novelties, but its latest addition to the new lifestyle is becoming an interesting target across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI for the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators.
It’s possible that BMW has attracted a lot of attention due to the controversies surrounding not just the fresh Neue Klasse models but also the previous lot of disconnected styling ideas. The Neue Klasse, meanwhile, unifies the design in just two directions: SUVs get a slim and vertical kidney grille treatment akin to older models, while passenger cars like the i3 and the latest 3 Series pack wide kidneys.
There has been much debate around the second-generation BMW i3, which has morphed into a classic sedan as the electric version of the 3 Series, and the Bavarians actually surprised everyone when the regular G50 model with ICE under the hood was presented looking almost the same as the EV models. The difference is subtle but visible – the G50 has better proportions due to additional space behind the front wheels, making it feel more planted.
It also helps that the new BMW M350 xDrive from the M Performance roster feels more like an M3 than ever – it even comes with 437 hp under the hood, which isn’t too far away from the G80 BMW M3 sedan’s base version, which packs 473 hp! The aero kit and the other goodies also make it a very good option, together with the grin-inducing BMW M Drift Moment feature, and it also doesn’t have the same harsh ride as the full M3.
Anyway, there are folks who still don’t appreciate the styling of the Neue Klasse BMW 3 Series even in M350 form, and a virtual artist has decided to find a solution to the predicament. Not long ago, the virtual artist Timur Altynbayev from Kazakhstan presented his unofficial, hypothetical M350 design project as a return to the E30 age with LED-infused small kidney grilles and dual round headlights, inadvertently also bringing back the beloved ‘ Angel Eyes .’
Those were a feature that appeared much later on the E90 series with factory halo/corona rings and evolved with the F30 into round-to-square LED angel eyes, while the fan base also equipped the E46 iteration with aftermarket LED or CCFL halo kits. Now, here’s also Nikita Chuicko, the virtual artist better known as " kelsonik " on social media, who thinks that now is the right CGI time to work on BMW's latest 3 Series (G50) with modern angel eyes.
So, he transforms the front bumper and also adapts the kidney grille to allow the placement of separate dual LED headlights equipped with LED angel eyes as daytime running lights, mirroring the F30 iteration while also taking some inspiration from the E30 series. Electric truck maker Harbinger has been racking up wins in recent months, and after scoring a $300 million order from international shipping giant FedEx and a defense contract with the US military, the company has drummed up another $240 million in Series D funding.
Companies like FedEx and Amazon have been making serious moves to fully electrify their fleet operations, both in an effort to decarbonize and to avoid the every-increasing price of diesel . At $300 million for 2,000 medium-duty electric delivery trucks, Harbinger’s latest deal with FedEx is believed to be one of the largest binding orders for electric medium or heavy-duty trucks in history – and it’s a big enough deal to inspire more than 240 million votes of confidence in the company’s future, one dollar at a time.
“Harbinger exists to challenge what industry has learned to accept, and reinvent the critical systems the world depends on,” said John Harris, the Co-Founder and CEO of Harbinger . “By rethinking critical systems from first principles, we aim to unlock better performance, greater reliability, safer operations, and more room to grow. Electrification is at the core of everything we do, and increasingly, electrification is at the core of industry, defense, mobility, and AI. Harbinger’s role is not simply to give customers another option. It is to reset expectations for what critical systems should deliver.”
Harbinger’s Series D funding round was co-led by Tiger Global, the Capricorn Technology Impact Fund, and Ridgeline. The company says the new funding will support expansion into energy storage systems, power generation, autonomy software, and defense applications , as well as the continued ramp up of its medium-duty platform manufacturing capacity. With this latest round of financing, Harbinger has raised over $650 million since 2021.

New Mansory Venatus Lamborghini Urus Is a One-of-One Egypt Special
20 photos
Photo: Instagram | _kourosh_mansory
Mansory has all kinds of new projects out, including the Lamborghini Urus pictured below, which is said to be a bespoke creation, and it is definitely a flashy ride. But then again, what did you expect from a one-of-one signed by this tuner?
The fender shields are on the special side of things. This machine is apparently called the Desert Ember, and also has Egypt in its name. That does not necessarily mean it’s a special commission from the former land of pharaohs, and to be honest, we do not know anything about this subject, because Mansory’s founder, who shared these images on social media a few days ago, hasn’t said much about it.
Starting on the outside, this tuned Lamborghini Urus, which is an SE , by the way, features fender flares, side skirt attachments, new mirror casings, and special trim on the front fenders. The hood is also new, and it is very aggressive, just like the OEM front bumper that has received numerous add-ons, including the flaps on the sides, the large blades attached to the splitter, and various other elements.
One wing was apparently not enough, so this Italian exotic crossover has two of them. One sits above the rear windscreen and the other below. There is also a three-piece ducktail spoiler on deck, as well as a very fat diffuser. The rear pillars have new trim on them, Mansory’s illuminated logo sits in the middle of the tailgate, and we can also see the new exhaust tips in the middle of the large diffuser.
Photo: Instagram | _kourosh_mansory This Lamborghini Urus SE has a satin gray look on the outside, joined by some orange accents, and the usual (for a Mansory) forged carbon trim. It rides on new wheels that have a two-tone look, mixing black and orange, and appears to sit a bit closer to the ground.
The bright orange accents are not there by accident, because this is the color that dominates the interior. You can see it on most touchable components on the inside, from the dashboard panel and center console, to the seats, steering wheel, door cards, pillars, and headliner. Even the seatbelts are presented in orange. The door cards have Mansory’s backlit logo on them, just like the emblems on the seatbacks, and the tuner’s logo can also be seen on a whole bunch of other components.
A good amount of carbon fiber trim is also on deck on the inside. This Lamborghini Urus SE features new pedal caps, new paddle shifters, and what seems to be a steering wheel that has come from the aftermarket world. The two screens, the buttons, air vents, and everything else, save for the ones that have been modded/replaced by Mansory during the tuning job, have come from the Sant’Agata Bolognese factory, which is where all Raging Bulls come to life, including the Urus.
Mansory’s founder says that this bespoke Lamborghini Urus SE has up to 1,085 horsepower (1,100 ps/809 kW) and 922 pound-feet (1,250 Nm) of torque in total. We do not know how fast it is, now what it’s new top speed is, because this information hasn’t been released at the time of writing. Nevertheless, the build in question has plenty of oomph to smoke the bone-stock version of the plug-in hybrid exotic crossover.
Photo: Instagram | _kourosh_mansory With zero modifications, the Lamborghini Urus SE hits 62 mph (100 kph) in 3.4 seconds, and can keep pushing up to 194 mph (312 kph). The plug-in hybrid 4.0-liter twin-turbocharged V8 engine steams out 789 hp (800 ps/589 kW) and 701 lb-ft (950 Nm) of torque combined. This means that Mansory’s Venatus SE is 296 hp (300 ps/331 kW) and 221 lb-ft (300 Nm) of torque more powerful.
Lamborghini’s new kid on the Urus block, the Urus SE Performante, comes with 801 hp (812 ps/598 kW) and 738 pound-feet (1,000 Nm) of torque straight from the factory. This Custom Sprinter Van Conversion Is a Luxurious Wellness Clinic on Wheels
23 photos
Photo: Vancini Conversions
Panel and cargo vans have proved their versatility time and time again. Apart from mobile living spaces, lately they have become a popular alternative to traditional business premises as well, offering the freedom to take a service directly to customers.
There are plenty of thriving mobile businesses that are operated out of a meticulously converted vehicle, from retail shops to healthcare clinics and specialized service businesses. Just like in the case of conventional camper vans, the possibilities are endless when it comes to transforming a van into a mobile workspace, but they are largely determined by the nature of the business and the creativity behind the conversion.
For their latest build, Vancini Conversions put their extensive expertise to work to create a mobile wellness clinic like no other. Designed and built for Calyx Drip, this custom van conversion is far from a basic mobile business; it’a a van built with intention.
Calyx Drip offers mobile IV therapy and medical-grade wellness services, and they needed a space that exudes warmth, calm, and professionalism; a space where clients can relax and rest assured they get professional, personalized care.
The idea was to add versatility to their operations, allowing them to provide their services on the go. With this mobile clinic, they can reach customers wherever they are.
Photo: Vancini Conversions Built inside a 2026 Mercedes-Benz Sprinter with a 170-inch wheelbase, this mobile clinic features a custom layout, specialized equipment, and carefully selected finishes that create a distinctly luxurious atmosphere inside. With custom leather reclining chairs, elegant curved LED lighting, and warm colors, the clinic will deliver wellness services in a setting that feels more like a high-end spa than a vehicle.
The base vehicle is a rear-wheel-drive Sprinter van powered by a 2.0-liter four-cylinder twin-turbo engine paired with a nine-speed automatic transmission. On the outside, it’s finished in elegant black with a full-custom branded wrap by Branded Wraps, which advertises the vehicle’s identity from a distance.
The team at Vancini Conversions equipped it with a 13.1-foot (4-meter) Fiamma F45S awning for some shaded space outside, as well as Atlas Roadcamp side and rear steps for easy entry. On top of the van, a Flatline Van Company roof rack holds 400 watts of solar panels, a Nomadic Cooling X3 12V air-conditioning unit, and a black Maxxair 7500K roof fan. The van also features some small AMA acrylic windows that can be opened from inside.
Photo: Vancini Conversions But what truly makes this van conversion stand out is its luxurious interior. The priorities of the van outfitter were quite different from when creating a mobile living space, but their craftsmanship and attention to detail still prevail. They leveraged the available square footage inside to create a functional space where the folks at Calyx Drip can provide quality services.
For a cozy, secure feel, the van has a closed-cab configuration, with a partition wall built by Vancini separating the driver’s area from the clinic. On that wall, they mounted a 55-inch LG 4K OLED TV, with access to it from the cab in case they need to replace it in the future.
The actual clinic space in the back is fitted with custom-stitched IV clinic chairs, long cabinets along each side of the van, and a rear bathroom. The arrangement is thought out to optimize efficiency and make tasks easy to perform.
Photo: Vancini Conversions The client wanted a warm ambiance inside, and Vancini created just that with a cohesive color scheme of light creams and wood tones, combined with durable, premium materials. The walls are made from flexible wood, finished with several coats of Italian limewash paint and a protective coating, giving the interior an upscale look, the cabinets are made from Baltic birch core laminated wood, and underfoot, they used stone-effect Lonseal flooring.
The gently curved ceiling incorporates recessed lighting, and Corian countertops add another elegant touch. Oatmeal-colored Marathon tweed upholstery was used around the rear door pillars, while brushed-gold accents can be observed on the custom-made Calyx Drip sign at the front, the baseboards, handles, sink, and faucet.
The client seats are custom-made reclining chairs from Premier Products, and though they have seatbelts, they are not meant to be used while the van is in motion. They are only meant for clients to settle in during their treatments. They are custom upholstered and feature the company’s logo stitched in.
Photo: Vancini Conversions Another nice detail is the custom CNC-cut, backlit logo on the passenger-side wall, which Vancini says it was designed in collaboration with Overland Interiors and was a very labor-intensive project.
The cabinets behind the client chairs are meant to keep specialized equipment and supplies organized, and a Vitrifrigo C51 refrigerator is also included. One of the cabinets has various drawers and open cubbies, and the other houses the components of the electrical system.
Photo: Vancini Conversions The day-to-day operations will be supported by a 920Ah heated Blizzard lithium battery bank, paired with a Victron MultiPlus-II 12/3000 inverter-charger, an Orion 50A DC-DC charger, a Victron 100/30 solar charge controller, and a Cerbo GX MK2 monitoring system with a GX Touch 70 display. Apart from the vehicle's alternator and rooftop solar panels, the batteries can also be charged via a 30-amp shore power connection.
A solid door leads to the rear bathroom, which is fitted with a Laveo Dryflush toilet, an overhead cabinet, a sink and faucet integrated into a custom-designed plumbing system. The van is also equipped with a 4kW Eberspächer diesel heater for a comfortable temperature inside.

Server Motherboards
ASRock Rack DMRD16-2L+ CPU and Memory
At OCP Summit 2026, ASRock Rack showed off its DMRD16-2L+. This is a single-socket board for Intel’s Diamond Rapids Xeon platform featuring sixteen-channel memory. The motherboard was also notable because it does not have standard PCIe CEM card slots and instead features all MCIO connectivity.
ASRock Rack DMRD16-2L+ Spotted with 16 DDR5 Slots for Diamond Rapids
This EEB board measures 12 inches by 13 inches and uses a single DIMM per channel (1DPC) layout across the sixteen slots. You can see that the socket is huge and has a neat cover. Instead of just pulling it off, you twist the socket cover to lock it in place.
ASRock Rack DMRD16-2L+ Motherboard Overview
ASRock Rack says it supports three module types: RDIMMs up to 128GB at max 8000MT/s, MRDIMMs up to 128GB at max 12800MT/s, and MRDIMM 2U modules up to 256GB, also rated for a maximum of 12800MT/s.
ASRock Rack DMRD16-2L+ CPU and Memory
On the board, we have lots of black MCIO x8 connectors on the I/O side. You can use up to 16x of these connectors across the board, each rated for PCIe 6.0 or CXL 3.0 at x8. So that is 128x PCIe Gen6 / CXL 3.0 lanes worth.
ASRock Rack DMRD16-2L+ MCIO Connectors
For local storage, there is a single M-key M.2 slot supporting PCIe 5.0 x4. It supports M.2 22110, 2280, and 2260 drives.
For management, ASRock Rack went with an ASPEED AST2700 BMC . There is also a dedicated IPMI port via Realtek RTL8211F and two RJ45 1GbE ports driven by an Intel I350 controller for basic network connectivity.
ASRock Rack DMRD16-2L+ ASPEED BMC
The rear I/O cluster includes two USB 3.2 Gen1 Type-A ports and a DB15 VGA connector. Two additional USB 3.2 Gen1 ports are available via an internal 19-pin header, alongside a separate internal video header, one COM header, and support for a 13-pin SPI TPM module.
ASRock Rack DMRD16-2L+ Rear IO and Management
Something neat here is that this does not have an OCP NIC 3.0 connector, nor traditional PCIe CEM slots. That means the server this goes into has all of its PCIe Gen6 I/O going through MCIO connectors. We have talked about PCIe signaling challenges since Ice Lake and Gen4, but with Gen6, we can see clear signs of the move to more cables.
Final Words
It is cool to see Intel’s Diamond Rapids architecture translated into physical hardware. The company has talked about sixteen channels for a while, but seeing it laid out on this single-socket board makes the design’s scale clear. With one DIMM per channel across two banks, you get all sixteen slots around a single CPU socket which is a lot.

This French Tiny House Is Perfectly Dreamy, Has the Best Built-in Porch
32 photos
Photo: Mon Reve en Bois
Anyone who thinks that the perfect tiny house doesn’t exist should take a closer look at this charming creation from an experienced builder in Occitania, France. A thoughtful layout makes it more spacious than the average mobile home in France, and that’s coupled with beautiful custom features, including a built-in porch, that elevate both beauty and comfort. Lastly, sustainable capabilities add to this home’s eco-friendly quality.
“Camarguaise” could be roughly translated as “the one from Camargue”, a beautiful river delta and coastal region in southern France. This is the name of one of the most impressive custom-builds by Mon Reve en Bois, an artisanal tiny house construction company located in Occitania (another French region famous for its idyllic landscapes).
Tiny house Camarguaise draws attentions immediately with its rounded roof extension, inspired by old gypsy wagons, and the built-in covered porch that brings to mind traditional family homes in the countryside. These two elements are enough to distinguish tiny house Camarguaise from any other French tiny house, but its size also makes an important difference.
Photo: Mon Reve en Bois While typical mobile homes in France don’t go past six meters in length (just under 20 feet), Camarguaise boasts a generous 7.3-meter (24 feet). Coupled with a 4-meter (13 feet), this allows for a flexible configuration with a ground-floor bedroom and a loft bedroom. Up to six people can be comfortably accommodated here, and amenities include a lovely dining setup with four seats. This is rare for a French tiny house made entirely of wood, and a great advantage.
Without a doubt, this tiny home’s built-in porch takes the spotlight. First of all, it’s big enough to actually be enjoyed as an outdoor living space, the perfect spot for the morning coffee or simply for watching the sunset. It’s also covered, which adds protection against the elements. Best of all, it’s beautifully crafted, including details such as the slatted fence on both sides, the thin pillars connecting the fence to the roof, and the wavy ornaments.
The rounded, wagon-inspired roof is the final detail that makes this porch extra charming, while the timber itself is the foundation, both literally and figuratively, of this lovely alternative to a conventional exterior deck. The fact that it’s built-in adds the advantage of less hassle, and truth be told, having a tiny home that can travel with its own porch is a great luxury in itself.
Photo: Mon Reve en Bois Even if this stunning porch was the Camarguaise’s only top selling point, it would be enough, but there’s more. From the porch, guests step right into the kitchen. The ground-floor has a wagon-like layout with the kitchen and dining area on each side, and a central corridor leading to the ground-floor bedroom.
This bedroom is unusual, compared to the typical ground-floor bedrooms you may have seen in other tiny homes. It comes in the form of an intimate nook or recess, which makes it much more bohemian and cozy than a plain bed sitting directly on the floor. The nook walls add privacy without isolating the room entirely. The nook itself also becomes a raised platform for the bed, with extra room for the bespoke corner shelves that act as romantic nightstands.
A big window right by the bed adds the luxury of superb views, while also filling this entire little recess with natural light. The ambiance is cozy and welcoming, and that extra bit of privacy is what makes this bedroom unique and dreamy.
Photo: Mon Reve en Bois Built-in closets that look almost invisible because they blend so well with the overall cabinetry add functionality to this area of the house. Everything here is custom-built, from the traditional kitchen cupboards to the bedroom closets and the staircase. This staircase deserves extra attention, as it showcases the same kind of woodwork mastery and clever craftsmanship as the built-in porch.
The quarter-turn or L-shaped design of this timber staircase is already unusual, especially for a tiny house, but surprisingly efficient in terms of saving space. It’s far more compact than other types of designs, yet multi-functional. All of the lower treads hide built-in drawers for storage, while the entire outer section, from floor to the loft landing, serves as a spacious pantry with wide, open shelves. All of this is achieved within a miniscule footprint.
The kitchen is typical for French tiny homes, boasting a relatively small countertop, but sufficient storage space for the basics and all the essential appliances (including a small fridge that fits under the counter). There was enough space on the other side for extra cupboards and a second countertop, but the builder chose a more practical alternative, namely a modern-style foldable breakfast bar.
Photo: Mon Reve en Bois The best part about this breakfast bar is the clever location, which allows room for up to four seats – an impressive number for a French tiny house. It’s also excellent that the bar is entirely foldable, which means that the entire area can be freed to make room for something else without much hassle. Lastly, with large windows both on this side and the kitchen side, this entire part of the house is filled with natural light and surrounded by nature views.
A fully-equipped bathroom completes this home’s functional layout, perfect for full-time accommodation and welcoming enough even for families. The enclosed shower cabin, the sink, and the vanity are part of the standard formula of a conventional bathroom, but the timber paneling throughout is one of the trademarks of artisanal French tiny homes – a mix of traditional and modern features that defines Tiny Camarguaise.
The loft bedroom, easily accessed via the quarter-turn staircase, flaunts a beautiful solid oak floor and large windows. It’s big enough for either a classic double bed or two single beds for young children, which adds to the flexibility of a layout with both a ground-floor bedroom option and a loft.
Photo: Mon Reve en Bois Described by its builder as a unique and bohemian mix between a tiny house and a wagon, for those who can’t decide between the two, Tiny Camarguaise offers the advantage of a tiny house layout with a loft and the dreamy charm of a gypsy wagon with a built-in porch. And that’s not all. A complete solar power kit makes it self-sufficient in terms of energy.
Adding to its eco-friendly and sustainable nature, Tiny Camarguaise also showcases the beauty and natural strength of locally-sourced timber. Its exterior cladding is made entirely of Douglas fir sourced locally from Occitania forests that are managed sustainably.
This specific type of wood has a high resinous content that makes it particularly resistant to insects and weather damage, as well as naturally water-repellant. An added layer of eco-friendly treatment makes this natural cladding even more durable, as well as low-maintenance.
Photo: Mon Reve en Bois Everything about Tiny Camarguaise speaks of natural living on multiple levels, from its choice of natural materials to the beautiful porch that invites its owners to spend more time outdoors. Boasting 37 square meters (just under 400 square feet) of floor space, and large windows throughout, this spacious house on wheels offers much more than the average French tiny home, without losing its uniqueness.
The fully-equipped, custom version of Tiny Camarguaise pictured in the gallery was delivered at a price of €58,516 ($65,250) – a great price, considering that it includes the off-grid kit as well, plus all the amenities and appliances. All in all, Tiny Camarguaise has all the qualities of a dream house, including a small price tag.

A California judge has deemed Tesla liable for fraud in a Solar Roof lawsuit, after the company repeatedly failed to hand over evidence. Tesla had already admitted it breached the contract, broke its warranty, and was negligent on the job.
The homeowner says fixing the damage will cost “well over $2.5 million.” Tesla once offered him $5,000.
The case is Conroy v. Tesla , filed in 2022 in San Diego Superior Court’s North County division (case No. 37-2022-00043670). Electrek reviewed the court orders, the complaint, and the parties’ joint trial readiness report. Here’s what’s in them.
Tesla has already admitted liability
Ambrose Conroy, who lives in Rancho Santa Fe, signed up for a Tesla Solar Roof in March 2020. The original contract was $82,210 for a 13.1 kW system. By February 2021, after two amendments, it had grown to roughly $110,000 for an 18.2 kW roof and six Powerwalls.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
The roof was never finished. It never passed a county inspection, and it never produced a single kWh for the house.
Tesla isn’t contesting most of that anymore. In the joint report filed by both sides last month, Tesla stipulated to liability on three of the five claims.
Joint Trial Readiness Conference Report, Oct. 20, 2026 (highlight by Electrek)
The other two claims, fraud and negligent misrepresentation, are where things went badly for Tesla.
Two sanctions, then the big one
Judge Cynthia Freeland sanctioned Tesla twice over discovery before going further. She ordered it to pay $15,467.50 in February and another $13,500 in June, both times for failing to produce a proper privilege log and responsive documents, and both times warning that issue sanctions could follow.
Tesla missed the next deadline anyway. So on September 11, the court deemed Tesla liable for fraud and negligent misrepresentation, limiting the trial on those claims to compensatory and punitive damages.
San Diego Superior Court minute order, Sept. 11, 2026 (highlight by Electrek)
The judge found “ample evidence to support that Defendants have acted willfully.” Among the missing records were Microsoft Teams messages (Tesla’s own corporate witness testified they’re kept “for infinity”), OSHA logs, emails with San Diego County inspectors, and more than 20 quality, install, and safety reports from Tesla’s internal Bolt system.
She also wrote this:
San Diego Superior Court minute order, Sept. 11, 2026 (highlight by Electrek)
Tesla asked her to reconsider, arguing it had since produced everything. She said no in a ruling dated October 27, writing that the late documents could support Conroy’s theory that Tesla “knowingly used Plaintiff’s home as an experiment while knowing they lacked the experience to perform as promised.”
Ruling on Tesla’s motion for reconsideration, Oct. 27, 2026 (highlight by Electrek)
“Experimenting” on the house, and daily reports to Elon Musk
And the “experiment” word shows up in Tesla’s own messages, according to the trial exhibit list. Exhibit 224 is described as text messages from January 13, 2021, between Tesla’s director of model engineering Bobby Yang and other Tesla employees.
Exhibit 224, joint exhibit list, Conroy v. Tesla (highlight by Electrek)
To be clear, that’s how Conroy’s side describes the messages on the exhibit list. We haven’t seen the texts themselves. But Elon Musk is on Conroy’s witness list, and internal emails quoted in the complaint point the same way.
On February 9, 2021, Yang wrote internally that the house was in the “99.5 percentile in terms of complexity” and that “if we can do this job well, we should be able to do any job well.” RJ Johnson, then head of Tesla’s energy business, replied that the project would “skew numbers” but that Tesla needed “to make it right.”
First Amended Complaint, Conroy v. Tesla (highlight by Electrek)
Then he added one more line.
First Amended Complaint, Conroy v. Tesla (highlight by Electrek)
Johnson was fired in April 2021. The roof had at least 59 mounting planes, and one employee called it the largest job Tesla had attempted at the time, according to the complaint.
A two-week job that never ended
Conroy’s account of the installation reads like a list of everything that can go wrong on a roof. These are his allegations, but Tesla has now conceded breach and negligence.
The tear-off was supposed to take two days and took two weeks. Tesla left in November 2020 with bare roof decking exposed, then had crews work overtime on December 27 to get underlayment down before a storm. Tiles arrived scratched and damaged and went on the roof anyway. Glass tiles shattered in the driveway and lawn, and the family says they still can’t walk there barefoot.
By March 2021, Johnson had agreed in writing that paying “when you’re happy with the outcome is completely reasonable.” Tesla’s billing department kept calling anyway.
In August 2021, an internal email weighed just leaving.
First Amended Complaint, Conroy v. Tesla (highlight by Electrek)
The project went through at least seven project managers. In November 2021, Tesla told Conroy the people behind its repair plan were gone and it had nobody in the area to do the work.
First Amended Complaint, Conroy v. Tesla (highlight by Electrek)
In April 2022, Tesla offered $5,000 to settle everything.
First Amended Complaint, Conroy v. Tesla (highlight by Electrek)
It didn’t end there. In February 2025, more than two years into the lawsuit, Tesla failed another San Diego County inspection after showing up without the plans for the venting system. And this summer, Conroy’s electrical expert opened up part of the roof and concluded that the way Tesla ran wiring and conduit under the tiles created a short-circuit and fire risk in heavy rain. The roof is now coming off. Tesla’s lawyers point out that even Conroy’s counsel called that fire risk “counterintuitive.”
Tesla wants the Court of Appeal to step in
Tesla is fighting the sanction hard. In an October 29 filing, it asked the court to freeze the case while it petitions the California Court of Appeal, arguing the order is “unduly punitive,” violates due process, and amounts to a directed verdict on fraud before trial.
Tesla also says the discovery fight had no connection to the fraud claims and that it has now produced everything relevant. The judge already rejected that argument once.
The November 20 trial date is off. A trial readiness conference is set for December 4, and Conroy’s lawyers want to go to trial in December.
This isn’t the first Solar Roof horror story in this case file. Conroy’s complaint attaches our 2020 report on a Solar Roof buyer left with tarps over his house after Tesla tried an untested underlayment on his home. It also cites a 2025 California Contractors State License Board action seeking to revoke Tesla’s contractor licenses over abandoned Solar Roof jobs.
Electrek’s Take
What a nightmare. This is the most damaging Solar Roof case I’ve seen, and I’ve been covering this product since Elon Musk unveiled it on a Universal Studios backlot in 2016.
A botched install isn’t news on its own. Tesla only installed about 3,000 of these roofs before killing the product this year, and plenty of them went sideways. What’s different here is the paper trail: internal emails calling a customer’s home a test of whether Tesla could do “any job,” texts describing the job as an “experiment” with daily reports going to Musk, and then years of Tesla failing to hand over its own records until a judge ran out of patience.
And Tesla’s response to all of it was $5,000.
Look, it’s normal for things not to go as planned with a new product, and early adopters need to be flexible. However, we are talking about someone’s literal roof over their head here and a trillion-dollar company. Tesla could have and should have made it right a long time ago.
The issue sanction might not survive the Court of Appeal. Courts don’t love deciding fraud through discovery orders, and Tesla’s due process argument isn’t frivolous. But even if it gets reversed, Tesla has still admitted it breached the contract and was negligent, and the jury will see how this customer was treated.
This also says a lot about how Tesla ran the Solar Roof business. It sold a product it knew was hard to install, on homes it knew were complex, while the people running the program kept leaving. Conroy’s house was one of the worst cases, but installers are still dealing with the fallout of Tesla walking away from the product earlier this year.
The real question is what’s in those Teams messages and texts Tesla fought so hard to keep out of this case. If this goes to trial in December, we might find out.

2026 SEMA Show • 2027 Toyota Crown Signia Gets GT-S Concept Treatment for SEMA, Becomes a Sleek Wagon
Dealer Trying To Sell 1970 Pontiac Trans Am With Only 36,000 Miles, Too Bad for the Upgrades
27 photos
Photo: eBay seller Consignify1
What a car. This 1970 Trans Am looks almost too good to be true, but unfortunately, the changes that it received, including the custom interior, are likely to make some people walk away.
The Trans Am wasn’t yet a thing in 1970. This was only the second year for the new Pontiac Firebird, but this specimen is here to demonstrate that the low production numbers didn’t mean the car wasn’t a desirable configuration.
In fact, the low production numbers make 1970 Trans Ams even more desirable today, and that’s another reason why stepping away from the day-one glory doesn’t make sense. However, this car is still an intriguing presence on the road, and I don’t think it’ll take long before it sells.
Photo: eBay seller Consignify1 Pontiac produced 48,739 Firebirds for the 1970 model year, and the Esprit was the most popular configuration, accounting for 18,961 orders. The base Firebird was the runner-up with 18,.874 units, and these numbers make perfect sense. These were the most affordable Firebird versions, and considering the 1970 model year came with new regulations and an increased focus on efficient engines, paying less for a new car was on the agenda for many Americans.
As a result, six-cylinder engines continued to be preferred over V8 configurations. In the base Firebird family, the six represented over 3,100 orders.
The Formula was third in buyers’ preferences, accounting for only 7,708 units. Only 3,196 Trans Ams ended up rolling off the assembly lines.
The Trans Am was standard with the L74 400 Ram Air III, and Pontiac offered two transmission options. Most people picked the manual, while 1,339 buyers went for an automatic.
Few people found the dealer-based method to get the optional Ram Air IV, so if you somehow come across a Trans Am with this engine under the hood, you’d better not miss the opportunity to buy it. Only 88 such cars were ordered, and 66 came with a manual transmission.
Photo: eBay seller Consignify1 The first thing I want to highlight about this 1970 Trans Am is the mileage on the clock.
The dealer claims the 36,000 miles you’ll notice when you look at the odometer is the actual mileage, so this Trans Am never spent much time on the road. It’s a garage-kept and well-maintained specimen, according to the dealer, which kind of explains its condition today, especially if no major repairs were involved.
I would still call the dealer and arrange a live inspection because there’s only one way to make sure that everything is as advertised. However, I would also ask questions about the previous ownership and the work this Trans Am has received, as I wouldn’t be surprised to learn that the paint is no longer original and the undersides have already been redone.
What we do know is that the cabin has been “tastefully upgraded,” as the dealer explains. The car is, therefore, sporting a custom black interior. I admit that it looks good, cozy, comfortable, you name it, but considering the low production numbers, I would have preferred a 1970 Trans Am with the original cabin.
This could make it harder for the car to find a new home, but eventually, someone will probably take it home, especially considering the engine under the hood.
It’s unclear if this is the original setup, but the Trans Am is fitted with a 400ci engine and an automatic transmission. No further specifics were shared, but the vehicle should be able to run and drive properly, meaning that taking it home doesn’t necessarily involve a trailer.
Photo: eBay seller Consignify1 Based on the photos shared on eBay, the Trans Am doesn’t require further investments, so it’s ready to be driven and admired at car shows. On the other hand, without all the big questions getting answers, I think that the only way to make sure you buy the right Trans Am is to call the dealer and go there in person.
Before you do this, you must convince your significant other that paying almost $50K for this car is worth it. The dealer wants $48,000, but considering the Make Offer option has also been enabled, you might be able to get a small discount if you’re committed to a purchase.
The listing will stay up for a few more weeks, and if you want to see the car in person, you’ll have to get a ticket to Naples, Florida. You should be able to avoid shipping costs, considering the car’s mechanical condition, obviously if you don’t mind the road trip back home.
We’re not being told anything about the papers, but a clean title should also be available. A 1970 Trans Am would be quite a museum piece if any original goodies are still around, including the build sheet and maybe other documents, so make sure you ask these questions when you go see the car with your own eyes.

2026 SEMA Show • Toyota Brings Fresh Adventure-Ready Concepts at the 2026 SEMA Show Under the Woodland Banner
Dealer Hopes To Get Over $50K for This Pontiac Trans Am, Price Actually Reduced
45 photos
Photo: Showdown Motors on eBay
Trans Am is the name, and 1979 is the model year. A combination that you really can’t ignore, especially considering what the 1979 model year represented for the evolution of the Pontiac Trans Am.
However, this specimen is no longer the all-original specimen that so many people would park in their garage. It’s a car whose only mission is to find a buyer and then be tucked away under a cover to only see the daylight on sunny Sundays.
The only problem could be the price. The dealer claims this is actually a discount, so if your negotiation skills are top-notch, maybe you can get an even better deal.
Photo: Showdown Motors on eBay Meanwhile, I can’t help but remind everybody out there that the 1979 model year was the year for the Trans Am. Pontiac celebrated the nameplate’s 10th anniversary, and the way it decided to do this made perfect sense.
The Tenth Anniversary Trans Am was, well, an anniversary model. It was the first configuration to cost more than $10K, but this made perfect sense. Every TATA came with every option in the entire lineup, so at the end of the day, you were getting fantastic value for the money.
Buyers could only choose the engine, with two options offered: the Pontiac 400 with a manual transmission and the Oldsmobile 403 with an automatic. This means that you can figure out what engine is under the hood by simply checking the transmission.
Photo: Showdown Motors on eBay While the production of the TATA was limited to 7,500 units, Pontiac ended the year with over 117K Trans Ams rolling off the assembly lines. It was the best year in the history of the Trans Am, and the timing was perfect, considering this was when it celebrated its 10th anniversary.
The base Firebird , which continues to be the most affordable version in the lineup, was the runner-up with 38,642 cars, followed by the Esprit with 30,853 units. The Formula was the least desirable, despite coming with a 301 two-barrel standard and the Trans Am engines optionally, with only 24,850 orders.
This Trans Am doesn’t sport the desirable TATA treatment, but the black package makes it a head-turning machine anyway. Before you ask, no, the paint is not original, as someone resprayed it before the car landed online.
The dealer doesn’t offer more specifics, but the Trans Am also sports a custom-painted bird on the hood and 17-inch wheels.
The cabin is also in almost perfect shape, and this makes perfect sense, considering everything in there is completely new. I don’t think you’ll find anything to complain about, and my recommendation is that you call the dealer and arrange an in-person inspection before you make an offer.
On the other hand, I believe that it’s a shame that this Trans Am has stepped away so far from the original configuration. While I’m a big fan of original vehicles, I’m not entirely against aftermarket upgrades, unless they don’t make much sense.
Photo: Showdown Motors on eBay This could be the case of the Pioneer radio in this Trans Am, though the seller reveals that it’s part of an upgraded audio system that also includes Pioneer speakers.
The car comes with a Hurst dual-gate shifter, power steering, and front power disc brakes.
As for the engine under the hood, the Trans Am is fitted with a 6.6-liter V8 paired with an automatic 3-speed transmission. It’s safe to assume that everything is in perfect shape, so if you want to hop in and drive, you should be able to do this during your live inspection.
Furthermore, I don’t think this Trans Am would require further investments, so if you’re the adventurous type, you can fly in and drive home in your new Pontiac. Just make sure it won’t be raining or anything, as it’d be a shame to damage this Trans Am after all these years.
Photo: Showdown Motors on eBay As for the price, this is where things are getting tricky. The vehicle doesn’t require further investments, but on the other hand, it also looks to be too expensive for someone who is in the market for a non-original car. Sure, it checks many boxes for an occasional driver, and that’s why I recommended that you go there in person, but many people might walk away when hearing how much this Trans Am costs.
The dealer wants $52,900 for this Trans Am, but they also enabled the Make Offer option on eBay, so call them and discuss the rest of the details if you’re interested in the car. A walkaround video would also come in handy, considering many other details are missing, especially regarding the underside.
The vehicle is parked in Fraser, Michigan, and considering the listing expires in 6 days, you should first convince your significant other that you need another Trans Am and then pack your bags for a trip to the dealer’s location to see the car with your own eyes.

Mercedes-Benz SLS Returns to CGI Life Without AMG Assistance, Perhaps That's the Right Virtual Idea
7 photos
Photo: car.design.trends / Instagram
The good folks over at Mercedes-Benz may have celebrated 140 years of innovation in 2026, but it’s pretty clear their sights are locked toward the future rather than the past – and their latest ideas attest to that.
Just recently, Mercedes-Benz has announced its latest innovations, and let’s just say that the screen craze is far from over in Stuttgart: from windows with integrated LEDs to windshields projecting holographic images, they found new ways to add pixels to their cars. Clearly, Mercedes is never shy about its love for massive screens.
However, more importantly, the new model assault will continue in the near future, and there are no plans to slow down in 2027. Instead, the latest report across the rumor mill states that the German automaker has plans to unleash at least seven new models by the end of next year, potentially even more.
The suspects include a new lease of life for the Mercedes-Benz A-Class with both hybrid and EV models planned; the eagerly anticipated ‘baby’ Mercedes-Benz G-Class, a smaller, more compact off-roader based on the MMA platform; six- and eight-cylinder models for the Mercedes-AMG C-Class; the Mercedes E-Class Electric acting as the EQE replacement; the ‘topless’ G-Class Cabriolet; a GLA Hybrid; plus the new GLC and GLC Coupe; and possibly others.
But, of course, even with this abundance of novelties, some folks are still not satisfied. One of them potentially resides across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI – a member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators. More precisely, the good folks over at " car.design.trends " have recently focused our attention on a hypothetical proposal for a brand-new Mercedes-Benz SLS by Augusto Fuchs.
The virtual artist, who is a Transportation Design Master at IED Torino and also a Surface Modeler and Designer for Airbus Helicopters, has a knack for automobiles, too, and recently envisioned the return of the SLS nameplate in the Mercedes-Benz lineup for his latest unofficial, hypothetical design project. Unlike the original Mercedes-Benz SLS AMG two-seat limited production sports car from the early 2010s, this time around there’s no mention of any AMG traits – and maybe that’s for the best.
After all, AMG is going wild recently with the GT 4-Door Coupe and GT SUV all-electric models, and there’s a ton of disgruntled fans who don’t appreciate the new styling, rather than the switch to an EV lifestyle. This digital SLS looks like a nice take on the recent Mercedes-Benz Vision Iconic concept, but adapted for a sportier take that remains elegant rather than extreme like an AMG.
So, what do you think – yay or nay? Would you buy something like that? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Car Design Trends (@car.design.trends)

2026 SEMA Show • This Batmobile-Looking Lamborghini Temerario Is on Display at SEMA
This Ford Mustang Costs Only $21K, Would You Buy It?
9 photos
Photo: Instagram | mxo.motors
Can you believe it’s been more than four years since Ford presented the S650 Mustang ? The seventh-generation muscle car was first presented at the 2022 North American International Auto Show, and production started the following year.
The model remains the only muscle car in production today to feature a V8 engine, and it is none other than the Coyote 5.0-liter unit that powers the GT and Dark Horse versions. It pumps out 480 and 500 horsepower (487-507 ps/ 358-373 kW), respectively. As for the Dark Horse SC, it has 795 hp (806 ps/593 kW) and 660 lb-ft (895 Nm) of torque on tap from its supercharged 5.2-liter V8, and needs less than 3 seconds to zip to 60 mph (97 kph).
Reports indicate that the modern-day Dodge Charger will go down the V8 route, presumably with the Hellcat engine being the biggest contender for the role, either toward the end of 2027 or maybe in 2028. As for the Chevrolet Camaro, it is said to return, presumably for the 2029 model year, and it is expected to feature a V8 option and an available stick shift. The next-gen Camaro is said to be offered as a four-door sedan only, so chances are there will be no traditional coupe.
Now, not all Ford Mustangs from this generation are strictly offered with a V8 engine, because as you already know, the most affordable trim levels utilize the EcoBoost unit. This is a 2.3-liter four-banger that produces 315 hp (319 ps/235 kW) and 350 pound-feet (475 Nm) of torque. The peak thrust is available at 3,000 rpm, and the maximum output at 5,500 rpm.
Photo: Instagram | mxo.motors The Ford Mustang EcoBoost from the S650 generation takes around 4.5 seconds to hit 60 mph (97 kph), albeit with the Performance Pack, because that time drops closer to the 5-second mark without it. The standing quarter mile takes over 13 seconds, albeit on a good day, and with a skilled driver behind the wheel.
Therefore, while the 2.3L EcoBoost may not be the engine of choice for petrolheads, not to mention that it’s not the most reliable one either, it definitely has enough grunt for daily drives, and the occasional thrashing on closed courses. But would you ever see yourself daily driving a Ford Mustang EcoBoost?
If you said yes, then the car pictured in the gallery above could be the one for your. It is a 2024 model year Ford Mustang EcoBoost that features a dark red paint finish on the outside, as well as a wing on the trunk lid, the GT logo between the taillights, four round exhaust tips, and some dark elements all around for a bit of contrast. The wheels are black, and we cannot really tell whether they are OEM or not.
Moreover, the dealer behind the ad, because this machine is for sale, as mentioned in the title, did not have much to say about it. The interior combines black leather and some cloth upholstery, and also features white stitching, some carbon-like trim, and the usual dual displays with their tablet-like design. It seems that the cockpit hasn’t been visited by the tuning fairy, unlike the exterior, which may trick some into thinking that they are looking at the V8-powered model.
Photo: Instagram | mxo.motors Other than some wear on the driver’s seat outer bolster, which is understandable for something like this, it seems that the 2024 Ford Mustang EcoBoost in question is in pristine condition. Sure, there could be some chips and scratches on the outside, but due to the images that accompany the listing, we cannot say anything about them.
According to the ad, the muscle car in question has in the region of 30,000 miles (~48,000 km) on the clock, so it has seen plenty of action. As for the how much it costs part of the story, we already told you (in the title) that you will have to fork out $21,000 if you want to buy this ride.
But assuming that you had over $20K and the desire to get a muscle car, would you really blow it on this four-pot S650 Ford Mustang, or would you get an older one with a V8 engine breathing air from behind the grille? If you said this one, then you know what to do next, don’t you?
By the way, the vendor is known as @mxo.motors on Instagram, and it’s not based in the United States, but in Iraq, and the Ford Mustang in question has been exported to that market from this side of the world. So, if you find yourself in the Middle Eastern country looking for an S650 Ford Mustang in the EcoBoost configuration, then you know what to do.
Before wrapping it up, we will remind you that the Ford Mustang EcoBoost Fastback has an MSRP of $32,995 in the States, whereas the Premium Fastback starts at $36,345. The GT Fastback, GT Premium Fastback, Dark Horse, and Dark Horse Premium have MSRPs of $47,800, $52,080, $65,080, and $70,075, respectively, whereas the Dark Horse SC kicks off at $106,090.
